events.title: Catherine Howard Is Executed
events.description: Catherine Howard, the fifth wife of King Henry VIII of England, was executed for adultery at the Tower of London. She was still a young woman when she died.
events.significance: Her fall was one of the most dramatic episodes of the Tudor court. It shows how dangerous royal marriage and court intrigue could be under Henry VIII.

events.title: Galileo Arrives in Rome to Face the Inquisition
events.description: The astronomer Galileo Galilei reached Rome to stand trial before the Inquisition. The charges concerned his defense of the Sun-centered model of the universe.
events.significance: The trial became a lasting symbol of the clash between scientific inquiry and institutional authority.

events.title: William and Mary Accept the Crown
events.description: After the Glorious Revolution, the English Parliament passed the Declaration of Right. It offered the crown to Mary Stuart and her husband William of Orange, who were then proclaimed joint monarchs.
events.significance: The settlement strengthened Parliament's power over the monarchy. It shaped later constitutional government in Britain and beyond.

events.title: The Massacre of Glencoe
events.description: At least thirty members of the MacDonald clan were killed in Glencoe, Scotland. The killers were soldiers who had been received as guests.
events.significance: The betrayal of Highland hospitality became one of the most infamous atrocities in Scottish history. It still echoes in Scottish memory and culture.

events.title: Amiriyah Shelter Bombing in Baghdad
events.description: During the Gulf War, US Air Force aircraft dropped two laser-guided bombs on an air-raid shelter in Baghdad. The shelter was believed to be a military command site, and at least 408 civilians were killed.
events.significance: The attack was one of the deadliest incidents of the war. It raised hard questions about precision weapons and civilian protection in modern warfare.
